title: Tag & Layer Setup
description: Create custom tags and layers, assign them, and prepare a scene for future scripting.
problemStatement:
**Goal:** Configure project‑wide settings for object identification.

1. Open **Edit → Project Settings → Tags and Layers**.
2. Add a new tag:
   - Under Tags, click the +, name it "Collectible".
3. Add two new layers:
   - User Layer 8: name it "Player".
   - User Layer 9: name it "Enemy".
4. In your scene (use the one from Task1 or create a new one), create a Sphere and name it "Gem". Set its tag to "Collectible".
5. Create a Cube named "Hero". Set its layer to "Player".
6. Create another Cube named "Monster". Set its layer to "Enemy".
7. Verify that the tags and layers appear in the dropdowns.
8. Take a screenshot showing the Inspector of the "Gem" with the "Collectible" tag visible.

Explain in one sentence: Why would we separate Player and Enemy into different layers?
hints: Layers are assigned at the top of the Inspector, tags just below the name field.
If layers don't appear immediately, you may need to close and reopen the Project Settings.
expectedOutput: Screenshot of the Gem's Inspector with tag 'Collectible'. Short answer: Layers allow us to control physics collisions and camera rendering per group.
